newsitem.title: GERMANY: Daimler sees profit, sales up "substantially" in 97.
newsitem.headline: Daimler sees profit, sales up "substantially" in 97.

text.p: German industrial giant Daimler-Benz AG should see "substantial" increases in operating profit and sales this year, building on a solid rebound to profitability in 1996, Chairman Juergen Schrempp said on Wednesday.

In a speech to be delivered at the company's annual general meeting, Schrempp said, "Although this year will be dominated by numerous product launches along with the implementation of programs to optimise business operations, we assume that we can achieve a substantial improvement in operating profit."
Schrempp added that sales for the year as a whole should be "substantially" above last year's 106.34 billion marks ($62.5 billion).
In the first four months of 1997, Daimler said group sales jumped 15 percent to 36.3 billion marks as all the company's major divisions posted higher turnover.
Schrempp also repeated his belief that Daimler will be able to achieve its goal of 12 percent return on capital employed within two years.
"The group is now active in businesses marked above all by healthy, self-sustaining growth and high profit potential," he said.
Daimler-Benz, Germany's largest company, reported an operating profit for 1996 of 2.423 billion marks, up from a loss of 7.197 billion marks in 1996.

Daimler-Benz's aerospace operations posted the fastest sales growth in the first four months of this year with turnover climbing 39 percent to 3.9 billion marks, largely on the back of its aircraft and space systems operations.
The backbone of Daimler-Benz, its Mercedes-Benz car and truck business, also showed double-digit sales growth between January and April this year.
Passenger car sales climbed 14 percent to 16.2 billion marks while commercial vehicle sales advanced 15 percent to 11.6 billion marks.
